title: Half the AI agents in production are if-statements with a GPU bill
why_read: A pointed critique of over-engineered AI agent systems in production, arguing many 'agents' are unnecessarily complex wrappers around logic that regex or simple code could handle.
analysis: The article argues that many production 'AI agent' systems are needlessly complex, citing a concrete example where an LLM is used to extract structured data (invoice numbers) that a simple regex handles more reliably and cheaply. It frames this as 'resume-driven AI engineering,' where flashy architectures (vector databases, multi-model orchestration) are chosen for appearances rather than genuine necessity, at the cost of latency, expense, and debuggability. This is a useful, grounded engineering critique that pushes back against AI hype with a practical cost/complexity lens relevant to anyone building production LLM systems.
